mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not underperform in periods where UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% quarter-over-quarter, combined with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10%, signals a broad-based supply contraction that depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO QoQ change < -3% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the monetary base (RSAFS) coupled with a simultaneous spike in the CPI inflation index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals an inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not underperform when both RSAFS contracts sharply and CPI exceeds 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months) signals improving consumer balance sheets, which boosts demand and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not outperform in periods where PAYEMS grows above 0.5% MoM for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% combined with accelerating wage growth (not directly observed, but proxy via PAYEMS growth > 0.7% MoM for two months) signals an overheating labor market, which increases inflation and policy risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a high-rate regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS > 0.7% MoM for two months AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not underperform when UNRATE falls below 4%, PAYEMS accelerates, and FEDFUNDS > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 8% quarter-over-quarter signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction and related industries and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL < 2%).
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not outperform when HOUST rises by more than 8% QoQ and CPIAUCSL remains below 2%.
